orgs.name: Philadelphia Office of Homeless Services — Homeless Intake Centers (Coordinated Entry)
services: GATEWAY / FRONT DOOR: this is the City's coordinated-entry system (CEA-BHRS). It assesses households and routes them to shelter, diversion and housing programs; it is the required entry point for City-funded shelter, not a charity that takes walk-in applications for cash aid.

Daytime intake centers (shelter/diversion assessment): Appletree Family Center, 1430 Cherry St. (215-686-7150); Roosevelt Darby Center, 804 N. Broad St. (215-685-3700); Veterans Multi-Service Center, 213-217 N. 4th St. (215-923-2600, Tue/Thu)

After-hours intake: Red Shield Family Residence (families), 715 N. Broad St., (215) 787-2887; Gaudenzia's House of Passage (single women), 111 N. 49th St., (267) 713-7778; Mike Hinson Resource Center (single men), 1701 W. Lehigh Ave., (267) 737-9099
Homelessness diversion: where funds permit, one-time help with move-in costs or rental assistance — priority to families with children at or below 30% of area median income (OHS diversion flyer)
No household can be denied shelter entrance for lack of identification
orgs.serves: People experiencing homelessness, and households at risk of losing their home, in Philadelphia
